rationale: Alameda County's 2026-27 secured bill for Oakland APN 3-5-3 displays a $3,000 MEAS-W OAKLAND VPT assessment. Oakland says VPT applies to qualifying properties in use fewer than 50 days during calendar 2025 and is collected on the following fiscal-year bill. This supports likely vacancy in 2025, but an assessment is not direct occupancy evidence; an exact start date and continuous spell are unknown.
vacancy_duration: Calendar year 2025 VPT classification: fewer than 50 days in use (at least 316 aggregate days outside use under the city's threshold), not necessarily continuous. Start date and 2026 occupancy unknown.

evidence.detail: The Alameda County Treasurer-Tax Collector account for the selected Oakland APN 3-5-3 shows a 2026-2027 secured bill, tracer 01387600, with a separate MEAS-W OAKLAND VPT charge of $3,000.00. The portal's rendered bill is labeled Internet Copy and says it is not an official bill. A sanitized excerpt is retained in scan/research_reports/noo42_2617_san_pablo_oakland_county_bill_excerpt.md.

Oakland describes VPT as applying to qualifying property in use fewer than 50 days during a calendar year; its FY 2026-2027 materials identify calendar year 2025 as the subject period and explain county collection on the following fiscal-year bill.
Oakland parcel GIS matches SORTPARCEL 003 000500300 to 2617 SAN PABLO AVE OAKLAND 94612 and use code 3200. This corroborates parcel identity, not physical occupancy.
The Berkeley property at the same street number is APN 054-1785-013-00 and is a separate city/ZIP and parcel; business and permit records for it were excluded from the Oakland occupancy assessment.

report_md: Verdict: likely_vacant (0.82). Alameda County's 2026-27 secured bill for Oakland APN 3-5-3 displays a $3,000 MEAS-W OAKLAND VPT assessment. Oakland's VPT standard indicates fewer than 50 days in use during calendar year 2025; this supports likely vacancy during 2025. It does not establish the actual move-out date, a continuous vacancy spell, or 2026 occupancy. The county bill display is labeled Internet Copy, not an official bill.
